facts.program: Affordable Heat Pump Program (Government of Yukon, income-based)
facts.claim: The Affordable Heat Pump Program helps low-to-median income households install an air-source heat pump. You must be approved before you install; anything installed before approval is not eligible. Apply for pre-approval with a Notice of Assessment for each adult and a Canada Child Benefit statement for each child. Approved households that heat with oil receive an upfront payment of $250 from Natural Resources Canada.
facts.amount: 100% of project costs up to $24,000, covering heat pump sizing, purchase and installation, electrical upgrades, integration of existing heating and required demand-management controls (not backup heating systems).
facts.eligibility: You own the home, it is your primary residence and at least 6 months old. Heat pump on NRCan's list of Cold Climate Air Source Heat Pumps for Manitoba and Yukon. Keep your existing heating as a backup; electric-heated homes must be enrolled in Yukon Energy's Peak Smart Home program. After-tax household income (line 23600 minus line 43500, all adults) of: 1 resident less than $53,820; 2 residents $110,400; 3 residents $139,150; 4 residents $163,300; 5 or more residents $184,000. Not eligible if you received funding from NRCan's Oil to Heat Pump Affordability program.
facts.dates: No closing date stated. Page dated May 13, 2026.

facts.program: Good Energy heat pump rebate (Government of Yukon)
facts.claim: Rebate for a heat pump in a home at least six months old. Rebate paid by cheque or e-transfer within 12 weeks. If your home is less than six months old, a different new-home heat pump rebate applies.
facts.amount: 50% of project costs up to $10,500 (sizing, purchase, installation, electrical upgrades, integration with existing heating and required controls; not backup systems).
facts.eligibility: Air-source heat pumps on NRCan's cold climate list for Manitoba and Yukon, or ENERGY STAR ground-source heat pumps. Homes with a non-electric system must keep it as backup. Homes with electric heat must keep it as backup and be enrolled in Yukon Energy's Peak Smart Home program.
facts.notes: Read in the browser on 2026-10-21. Funded in part by the federal Low Carbon Economy Fund.

facts.program: Good Energy wood heating rebate (Government of Yukon)
facts.claim: Rebate for installing a qualifying wood heating system (boiler, cordwood stove, fireplace insert, furnace or pellet stove) in a building at least 5 years old.
facts.eligibility: EPA-listed and meeting emission limits (EPA New Source Performance Standards or CSA B415.10).

facts.program: Good Energy insulation and air sealing rebates (Government of Yukon)
facts.claim: Rebates for insulation in an existing home (5 years or older) and for air sealing. An energy assessment is required first, and a follow-up assessment after the work (a fee applies for each post-renovation assessment). Above-ground wall rebates are proportional to the wall area you insulate, below-ground rebates to depth up to 6 feet, and attic and slab rebates to the share of area insulated.
facts.amount: Up to $12,000 for insulating above-ground walls (you must at least double the existing level). Up to $10,000 for below-ground walls. $2,000 for slabs or floor systems. $2,500 for the attic (existing level R40 or less, increased to R60 or more). Air sealing $5,000 per building when the air sealing target is met (at least 3 air changes per hour before, 1.5 or fewer after, and an HRV installed).
facts.eligibility: Home 5 years or older. Below-ground walls and slabs: existing level R20 or less and an increase of at least R20.

facts.program: Good Energy ENERGY STAR window rebate (Government of Yukon)
facts.claim: Rebate for complete ENERGY STAR certified window assemblies installed in a heated building at least five years old. Sealed or insulated glass units alone are not eligible.
facts.amount: $120 per window up to $1,800 per home or building.
facts.eligibility: ENERGY STAR documentation for each window.
facts.notes: Read in the browser on 2026-10-21. Rebate paid within 12 weeks.

facts.program: Dependable Grid Program rebates (Government of Yukon)
facts.claim: Rebates to install non-electric heating and cut winter electricity demand, for new homes and homes with electric heat. Launched April 2026. You do not need to remove the existing electric heating.
facts.amount: Primary non-electric heating system (oil or propane): 50% of costs up to $15,000 for existing homes, $15,000 for new homes. Secondary non-electric backup (oil, propane or wood): 50% up to $5,000 existing, $3,000 new. Dual fuel (energy efficient heat pump plus a non-electric backup that works in a power outage): 50% up to $15,000 existing, $15,000 new.
facts.eligibility: Existing homes need an installed electric heating system. Apply through the rebate portal with itemized invoices, proof of payment, inspection reports and photos.
facts.dates: No closing date stated. Work must start after April 1, 2026 unless stated otherwise.
facts.notes: Read in the browser on 2026-10-21. The April 1, 2026 start date comes from a Yukon news release, not this page.

facts.claim: Low-cost funding for homeowners who complete qualifying energy upgrades, paid back through a local improvement tax.
facts.amount: Based on 25% of the property's assessed value, up to $50,000.
facts.eligibility: Qualifying energy upgrades to residential buildings.
